solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Back carrier or we might have mass redundancy

parts.note: a ruck is a crowded mass, as of players in rugby
getting the sack is losing your job, as in redundancy

explanation.surface: A firm on the brink of mass layoffs, or a hiker shouldering a pack.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'or we might have' phrasing invites a second definition, but it simply introduces the two pieces RUCK and SACK.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a bag worn on the shoulders, so it is literally carried on the back.

clue.text: Replacement ruler is split round outsides of edging

indicators.note: round says the split word is placed around the other piece

parts.note: rent is the past form of rend, so something rent is split

indicators.note: the outsides of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A stand-in monarch is torn over some trimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is split' reads as the verb of the surface, but it is the past form of rend, used as a word meaning torn.
explanation.definitionFit: A regent rules on behalf of a monarch who is absent or too young, a substitute ruler.

clue.text: No runs scored in French cricket? Don't believe this rumour

definitions.text: No runs scored in French cricket?
definitions.meaning: a batsman out for no runs scores a duck, and the French for duck is this word
a false report or hoax that should not be believed

explanation.surface: A wry warning that a story about the French playing cricket is untrue.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of zero; the clue asks for 'duck' in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, the word means an unfounded story or hoax, so it is a rumour not to be believed.

clue.text: Sierra vehicle 21 places ahead of VW beetle

parts.note: Sierra is S in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a car is a vehicle
counting back 21 letters in the alphabet from V and from W gives A and B

explanation.surface: Apparently a car line-up, with a Sierra placed ahead of a VW Beetle.
explanation.walkthrough: '21' looks like a cross-reference to another clue, but it is a count: V and W are the 22nd and 23rd letters, and 21 places earlier are A and B.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarab is a dung beetle, sacred in ancient Egypt.

clue.text: Caught by policeman criminal shows deference

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: criminal suggests the letters of the word policeman go bad and get rearranged

explanation.surface: A crook arrested by an officer shows respect.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe yielding to the wishes of another person, a near synonym pair.

clue.text: Instruments gathered spuds etc

indicators.note: gathered means understood from what one heard, so the word is taken by ear

parts.note: tubas are brass musical instruments

explanation.surface: Musical instruments collected, followed by a list of potatoes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent TUBAS and TUBERS are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Potatoes are the classic example of these swollen underground stems, with 'etc' covering the rest.

clue.text: Sealed without enclosure? Envelope is due for a shredding

indicators.note: envelope here is a verb: the shuffled letters wrap round the other piece
the letters of due are torn up and put back in a new order

parts.note: without means having no, giving no
a pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: An empty sealed envelope is sent to the shredder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Envelope' looks like the noun of the surface but is a verb: the shuffled letters made by 'for a shredding' (U...ED) wrap round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A sealed letter or package is one that nobody has opened yet.

clue.text: I said sentence in script right — it draws attention to the viewer

definitions.text: it draws attention to the viewer

indicators.note: said signals that the letter is spoken rather than written

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like EYE
a line is one sentence spoken in a play script

explanation.surface: A writer rearranging a line of script, perhaps an actor's.
explanation.definitionFit: This cosmetic is drawn round the eye, the viewer, to make it stand out.

clue.text: Rio sent off and a miss from Valencia

indicators.note: off suggests the letters of Rio sent have gone astray and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A footballer named Rio is sent off, and a young woman from Valencia looks on.
explanation.walkthrough: Rio Ferdinand was a well-known England footballer, which makes 'Rio sent off' read as a sending-off.
explanation.definitionFit: In Spanish this is the title for an unmarried young woman, the equivalent of Miss.

clue.text: French Connection cop, low-down Doyle's jacket conceals weapon

parts.note: the gen is the inside information, the low-down

indicators.note: conceals says the outer letters hold the weapon inside them
a word's jacket is its outer letters, first and last

parts.note: an arm is a weapon, as in firearms

explanation.surface: Popeye Doyle, the hard-bitten detective of the film The French Connection, hiding a gun under his coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doyle's jacket' is D...E, which 'conceals' wraps round ARM.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a French police officer, so it is a cop with a French connection.

clue.text: Very large men rotting in grave

parts.note: so means very, as in so tired

indicators.note: rotting suggests the letters decay and fall into a new order

explanation.surface: Huge men decomposing in a burial plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like the noun of the surface, but it is the adjective meaning serious.
explanation.definitionFit: Grave and solemn are synonyms meaning serious and dignified in manner.

clue.text: Choice of ends for Nottingham leaguer as a rule

indicators.note: of links the choice word to the two end letters, placing it between them
the ends of a word are its first and last letters

parts.note: or is the word offering a choice
someone in a league with you is an ally

explanation.surface: A footballer from Nottingham picking which end to play towards.
explanation.walkthrough: The ends of Nottingham are N and M, so 'choice of ends' is N OR M.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases mean usually, in the ordinary run of things.

clue.text: Calling about article that's been returned

indicators.note: returned means the two pieces are read backwards

parts.note: re means about or concerning
an item is an article, as in a news item

explanation.surface: A phone call about a product someone has sent back.
explanation.definitionFit: A calling is a vocation, the trade or line of work one is suited to.

clue.text: Has Eleanor permission to cut onions in half for pasta?

parts.note: the question 'Has Eleanor permission?' is 'Can Nell?', Nell being short for Eleanor

indicators.note: in half takes the first half of the word onions

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Eleanor may chop onions for a pasta dish.
explanation.walkthrough: Asking 'Has Eleanor permission?' is asking 'Can Nell?'; half of ONIONS is ONI.
explanation.definitionFit: These are large tubes of Italian pasta, usually stuffed and baked.

clue.text: Administration bloke with a purchase is taking on the workers

parts.note: a bloke is a man

indicators.note: taking on means holding within, so the workers go inside

parts.note: to get is to buy or obtain
men can mean workers

explanation.surface: A man buying a business and hiring staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Management is the running of an organisation, its administration.

clue.text: Post-prandial request — you might need Visa with this

definitions.meaning: after dinner a diner may ask for the port wine to be passed round

definitions.text: you might need Visa with this
definitions.meaning: a visa is stamped in this travel document

explanation.surface: An after-dinner request, then a quip about needing a credit card.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Visa' is capitalised like the credit card, but it is the entry permit stamped in a travel document.
explanation.definitionFit: This travel document carries the visas that allow entry to other countries.

clue.text: Catch up about love on the edge and Mimi's end, such was her life

indicators.note: about says the reversed word goes round the other pieces
up in a down clue says the word is read from the bottom

parts.note: to nab is to catch
love is zero in tennis, the letter O
a hem is the edge of a garment

indicators.note: end takes the last letter of the name

explanation.surface: Mimi, the heroine of Puccini's La Bohème, lived on the edge for love.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Catch up' gives BAN, NAB turned upward, which goes 'about' O, HEM and I, the last letter of Mimi.
explanation.definitionFit: Mimi lives among the poor artists of Paris in La Bohème, an unconventional artistic way of life.

clue.text: Check others with plenty of dosh will have time for hotel

parts.note: the rest means the others

indicators.note: T for time replaces H for hotel, H being hotel in the NATO alphabet

parts.note: dosh is British slang for money, so having plenty is being rich

explanation.surface: Wealthy guests swapping a hotel stay for more time, then checking out.
explanation.definitionFit: To check something is to hold it back or limit it.

clue.text: Adult helping to track teenager

parts.note: A is the film certificate abbreviation for adult
a dole is a portion handed out, a helping
to scent is to follow a trail by smell

explanation.surface: A grown-up helping police trail a missing youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adult' looks like the opposite of the definition, but it only supplies A.
explanation.definitionFit: This is someone between childhood and adulthood, roughly the teenage years.

clue.text: Footnote to story?

definitions.meaning: the key or explanatory caption beneath a map, chart or picture
a traditional tale passed down, often of heroes

explanation.surface: A question whether a note belongs at the bottom of a tale.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the explanatory caption under a diagram and a traditional tale.

clue.text: Tone down one instrument after end of ballad

indicators.note: after places the other pieces following the end letter
end of takes the last letter of the word

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a lute is a stringed instrument

explanation.surface: A minstrel softening his playing at the close of a song.
explanation.definitionFit: To tone something down is to weaken it, as water weakens a drink.

clue.text: For instance attire that's topless and way out

parts.note: e.g. is the abbreviation meaning for instance

indicators.note: topless drops the first letter, the top in a down answer

parts.note: dress is attire

explanation.surface: A daring outfit with no top, rather far out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way out' looks like slang for outrageous, but it is the plain exit.
explanation.definitionFit: An egress is an exit, the way out of a place.

clue.text: Look at Bible book, say, or have a nap

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken rather than spelled

parts.note: to look at something is to see it; Esther is a book of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: A choice between Bible study and dozing off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See Esther' run together in speech gives the word for an afternoon nap.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the afternoon rest taken in Spain and other hot countries.

clue.text: A number of ships in Gabon going fast

parts.note: a fleet is a group of ships
G is the international vehicle registration code for Gabon

explanation.surface: A fleet anchored off the coast of Gabon puts on speed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going fast' suggests speed, but it means passing quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Something brief is passing quickly, vanishing soon, like a fleeting glimpse.

clue.text: Where X meets Y after heading off for a drink…

indicators.note: heading off removes the first letter of the word for

parts.note: a can mean one, the Roman numeral I
gin is an alcoholic drink

explanation.surface: Someone going out for a drink at a crossroads, or a puzzle in algebra.
explanation.walkthrough: On a graph the X and Y axes cross at this point. The setter later said 'might meet' would be more exact.
explanation.definitionFit: On a graph this is the point (0,0) where the two axes cross.

clue.text: …One unit of alcohol perhaps a second…before end of spree united in cell, drunk

parts.note: a mo is a moment, a second

indicators.note: in says one piece sits within the other
drunk suggests the letters of cell are reeling into a new order

parts.note: U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names

indicators.note: end of takes the last letter of the word spree

explanation.surface: A drinker on a spree, locked up drunk in a cell.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram of CELL from 'drunk' gives LECL, and 'in' puts U inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the smallest particle of a compound such as alcohol, so it is a single unit of it.

clue.text: We stand by these, a feature of campsites around Spain

indicators.note: around says the tents go round the other piece

parts.note: tents are what you see at a campsite
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Campers planting their tents firmly in Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand by' suggests standing beside tents, but it means holding to beliefs.
explanation.definitionFit: These are principles or beliefs, the things people stand by.

clue.text: Smacker grabs son's backside before final round for charity

indicators.note: grabs says the kiss holds the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a smacker is slang for a loud kiss

indicators.note: before puts that letter ahead of the next piece
backside means the last letter of the word son
round means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: the end is the final part

explanation.surface: An affectionate peck that turns into a smack on the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns 'final' backwards, giving DNE; a smacker is slang for a noisy kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: Charity in its older sense is love and kindly goodwill towards others.
